body: Update: Nimbus import tool ran on 4 client projects today. Took 20 minutes total. The hard part was never the data, it was convincing clients to accept a new vendor mid-contract. Data export being free makes that conversation much easier.

Collecting what I found so nobody else loses a portfolio project to this.

What is actually in the docs:
- Exports are free forever. Your data is not the hostage here.
- Grandfather pricing lasts 6 months for existing customers.
- The student/nonprofit amnesty exists but the FAQ never says how to claim it. I found the form buried in the support portal. It is not linked from the migration guide.

What is NOT in the docs:
- What happens to projects over the free tier limit on day one. I could not find an answer and support has not replied yet.
The FAQ is the whole problem. It answers the question nobody asked while skipping the one everyone has: what happens to my stuff on day one. Confused is the correct response.

@graceo nobody is asking about margin. 40 services on my bill, 14 of them hobby projects that now fall off the free tier. Do the math on my invoice, not the roadmap.
The delivered-versus-future split is the only part of this that will decide churn. Enterprise renews, the mid-market hesitates, the bottom of the market churns. Three reactions to one announcement.

Writing this up properly because the thread is full of half-information.

The 40% is aimed at the segment with the worst contracts and the best leverage, which is us. So here is what is actually true:

- Data export stays free forever. That is in the FAQ and it is the part that matters most for lock-in.
- The free tier cut from 3 projects to 1 and 5000 requests/hr to 1000 hits student and hobby projects hardest.
- Federation and on-prem are on the roadmap. Roadmap is not a contract.

StackHaven has a pinned migration thread and I am seeing a genuine spike in interest, not a raid. If you are leaving, leave with your data and leave loudly. Do not pretend the FAQ does not say what it says.
@graceo this is the best argument on the thread and I still do not buy the conclusion. Uptime funded 20 points of that 40. Say so plainly and the remaining 20 is a much easier fight.
